title: The story of the teddy bear
text:
The teddy bear is one of the most popular toys in the world, and its history begins in 1902 with a famous politician. In November of that year President Theodore Roosevelt travelled to Mississippi {A}. His companions had been unsuccessful for days, so they caught a young black bear and tied it to a tree, hoping that the President would shoot it. Roosevelt refused, {B}.

A cartoonist named Clifford Berryman drew the scene for a Washington newspaper, and the picture was reprinted across the country. A shop owner in Brooklyn, Morris Michtom, saw the cartoon. He and his wife made a soft toy bear and put it in the window {C}. They asked the President for permission to use his name. The answer was yes, and the toys quickly sold out.

Meanwhile, in Germany, a company founded by Margarete Steiff had produced a similar bear independently. At the Leipzig Fair in 1903 an American buyer was so impressed that he ordered three thousand {D}. Within a few years bears were being made by dozens of factories in both countries.

Today collectors pay thousands of pounds for early bears {E}. Many people keep the toy of their childhood for life, and some hospitals give bears to young patients, because children feel calmer when they have something soft to hold. For a toy that was invented by accident, {F}.
